title: An Audience at Vantor
lead: An invitation has come from the Serene Regent, in plain white, on real paper. It offers safe passage, a private audience, and the answer to one question of your choosing.

gm.truth: The Regent keeps their word exactly. They know everything except how the Roster ends. Each Regent reads a letter on taking office, in the hand of the first: 'We hold this seat until the Sovereign wakes, and our whole duty is that it shall not.' The Regency was founded 1,006 years ago by the Order of Ilun's own Proctors, who pulled singers back with blades that drink energy. They decided Resonants were the noise that would wake it, left the Order and built a state to silence every one of them. A regent rules in the name of someone who can't, and nobody has ever asked in whose name. The shipments aren't a bribe: 'The Regency calls it a tax, because a tax pays for something.' The Regent wants three things from the captain: the fleet's people as coin, which buys Vantor perhaps a year; the fleet kept away from the Harbor, since they believe the noise of a fleet full of Resonants at the Shoal's edge would wake it; and Voss, the one walker the Choir ever let go on purpose, as proof it can be dealt with. They also offer the captain the succession. No Regent has an heir, and this one has been looking for someone who can do sums. They're wrong about three things, and those are the only things that can shake them. The Cantor has never heard of them: 'We thought they were pilgrims. We thanked them.' The evening chimes, which they believe are a receipt saying this world is paid up, are a line from the old watch call: OFF WATCH, DO NOT DISTURB. The silver has always gone round Vantor for that reason, and the tax has never bought anything. And the Maris record shows it doesn't wake from noise. It wakes from boredom, so a thousand years of silencing Resonants has been starving the song of singers. If the captain can show all this, the Regent will be silent for a very long time. Then they'll ask who wants to stop paying, to test it, with two billion people on the line. Arc clues: regency_letter, cantor_no_deal, evening_chimes, boredom_not_noise, token_names.
beats: Vantor: lemon polish and nothing else. White towers, trams on time, everyone polite, and a courtesy escort who apologizes for each camera by name. It's the first city the captain has seen in seven months where people aren't afraid of the Choir, because they have no idea. At dusk the chimes begin, and everyone goes home.
The audience. A plain white room. A small old person in plain white pours the tea. 'The Regency has read your file. Ask your question.' They mean one question, and they'll answer it fully.

The letter. The Regent shows it if the question comes anywhere near it. They explain the arithmetic as if discussing the weather, and they open a long drawer of silver discs to show that the books balance. It's the first time anyone has told the captain the whole truth without being asked twice, and it's the worst thing they've ever heard.
The offer: a seat, an heir's seal and a number. The number is how many people it would take to make everything all right for a while.

The captain answers. Try to kill them, try to show them they're wrong, accept, lie or walk out under safe conduct, which will be honored to the second and not a second beyond. Ministry Blades wait politely at the far edge of that second.
routes: Talker: argue it, with evidence (persuasion, lore, science). Bring the Cantor's words, the Maris core and the chimes laid out against the Codex. No one has ever told the Regent they were wrong and had the numbers. It's the only fight they might lose.

Deceiver: accept, or seem to (deception, composure). Take the heir's seal, walk the inner court and read the archive. The Regent will assume you're lying, it will amuse them, and they'll let you go on until it stops being useful.

Infiltrator or hacker: while the captain's in the white room, someone else is in the Ministry's archive or on the Evening Line (hacking, stealth), with Vael's or Corvane's codes if they've got them. The letter's original, the Stillness Engine plans and the full manifests are all there.

Fighter: assassination is possible. The Regent is no fighter, and there are only two guards in the room (firearms, melee). Run the consequences at full weight: a successor emerges within hours, every Blade in the Hegemony comes after the captain, and everyone waits to see if the silver follows.

Resonant: stand in the square for the chimes (attunement), and hear what they're really saying. The Regent has no Resonance at all. They're terrified in the way a glacier is cold: all the way through, and for a long time. That's a thing you can say to them.
checks: persuasion:very_hard to make the Regent stop and think
lore:hard to read the chimes against the old watch call
composure:hard to drink the tea and keep your hand steady
deception:very_hard to take the seal and be believed
stealth:hard to reach the Ministry archive with an escort on your heels
hacking:very_hard to pull the founding letter from the Ministry's sealed files
fights: ministry_blade and hegemony_trooper once the safe conduct expires, or sooner if the captain reaches for a weapon
outcomes: If the Regent is shaken, the shipments go on while they do new sums. They may join a last-ditch alliance, or send a squadron to the Harbor anyway, either with total calm. They'll speak to the captain again, which almost no one has managed.

If the Regent is killed, there's a successor by morning, and the Hegemony fractures. Vael, Halloran and others are freed or purged. Vantor becomes a real moral problem: two billion people who've just found out what they've been paying for.
If the captain accepts the succession, it's the game's darkest road (see The Regent's Peace). It stays possible to turn on it later, for a while.
If they walk out, the Hegemony moves openly: blockade, Blades at Sarn, and a squadron mustering to reach the Harbor first.
If the captain learns the chimes, they've learned a very dangerous trick: anyone could ring that pattern, and the silver would pass by. What happens to the song, if everyone goes off watch?
gm.rewards: A copy of the founding letter on a data_chip, the Regent's respect, and the plans for a Stillness Engine if anyone reached the archive. A ministry_saber only by taking it.
